statement: What is the last digit of 3^2026 + 7^2026?

choices.misconception: I added the last digits of 3 and 7 to get 10 without raising them to the power.
I multiplied the two last digits, 9 x 9 = 81, instead of adding them.
I treated 2026 as a multiple of 4, so both powers ended in 1.
I found the last digit of 3^2026 only and forgot to add 7^2026.

hints: Last digits of powers repeat in short cycles.
Find the cycle of last digits for powers of 3 and for powers of 7, locate the exponent by its remainder on division by the cycle length, and add the two last digits.
Powers of 3 end 3, 9, 7, 1; powers of 7 end 7, 9, 3, 1. Both cycles have length 4, and 2026 = 4 x 506 + 2.

solutions.reliable: Powers of 3 end in 3, 9, 7, 1, repeating every 4. Powers of 7 end in 7, 9, 3, 1, also every 4. Since 2026 leaves remainder 2 on division by 4, both powers end in the second entry, 9. Then 9 + 9 = 18 ends in 8. The transferable idea: reduce the exponent modulo the cycle length, find each last digit, and only then combine.
solutions.elegant: 3^2026 + 7^2026 = 9^1013 + 49^1013, and both 9^1013 and 49^1013 end in 9 because odd powers of a number ending in 9 end in 9.

whyOnTest: Last-digit cycles are a 3-point staple; the question checks that you combine the digits only after finding each one.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
